thread:
Chris: Quick sync — I'm sketching a v2 rollout metadata shape. Main idea: add a visibility scope for pins (global | tenant | ephemeral) and make TTL semantics explicit. Need thoughts on backward compatibility across Hosted / Dedicated / Private and on what guarantees we give clients when TTLs lapse. Draft below.
Ada: +1 on explicit scopes. One immediate question: do we treat TTL expiry as a GC hint or an authoritative eviction? I think we need both: a soft_ttl (hint) and a hard_ttl (eviction).
Megan: soft/hard split makes sense. Soft = eligible for eviction / deprioritize; hard = cannot be selected. Also want a short "grace_window_seconds" so we can surface client rollbacks.
Rishi: For routing, if soft_ttl passed we should avoid routing unless route policy includes "prefer_fresh". Also important: telemetry for soft->hard transitions so SRE can see regressions.
Samir: Edge case: tenant pin overrides a global pin. Precedence rules matter. Proposal: tenant_override > tenant_pin > global_pin > default. We should encode a "precedence" hint in metadata to avoid ambiguous merges.
Ada: To keep wire small, propose keys: visibility, soft_ttl, hard_ttl, origin, affinity_priority. origin can be 'canary', 'manual', 'auto-rollout'.
Megan: Add operational fields: rewrite_reason, origin_version (model commit hash), and an optional human_note for support teams.
Chris: How about schema evolution? We should use compact names on the wire but map to verbose names in the console. Also default server behavior must be old-behavior when fields absent.
Rishi: SDK compatibility note — older clients will ignore unknown keys but might assume old TTL semantics. Plan: server enforces constraints and offers a feature-flag header x-pin-schema-version so clients can opt in to v2 semantics.
infra-bot: deploybot: pin-schema-v2 config rollout scheduled for 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z (canary -> global). Will emit a warning header when serving older-client flows.
Samir: Action items: 1) compatibility test matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private + SDK versions), 2) migration runbook for tenants with active pins, 3) telemetry dashboard for TTL expirations and precedence overrides.
Ada: I'll draft a short RFC PR with the compact JSON template + runbook. Assigning to myself — will include a backward-compatibility checklist.
Chris: Great. @Megan can you paste a compact JSON sample here so we can iterate on field names?
Megan: Sure — example:
```
{
  "v": 2,
  "visibility": "tenant",
  "s_ttl": 86400,
  "h_ttl": 172800,
  "origin": "canary",
  "aff": 10,
  "origin_ver": "c3f9a7b",
  "note": "migrated from legacy pins",
  "precedence": "tenant_override"
}
```
Ada: Love the compact keys (s_ttl/h_ttl). Minor ask: rename "aff" -> "aff_pri" so it's clearer in logs.
Rishi: Also add a small boolean "client_probe_safe": true/false to indicate whether older clients can probe safely without triggering eviction behavior.
Samir: We'll need a migration job that backfills precedence for existing pins — I'll draft the query and a dry-run plan.
Chris: Good thread. Next step: Ada PR, Samir migration dry-run, Rishi telemetry dashboards. :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack-style thread about rollout metadata schema, TTL semantics, visibility scopes, and compatibility action items. Contains a short JSON code sample.
